title: Study strategies for dyslexia
examples: What is the best way to read a textbook chapter?
Can technology help people with dyslexia?
How can I remember things better when I have dyslexia?

explain.say: Today we are learning some great ways to study when reading is tricky.

items: Step 3: Listen to the computer read it

explain.say: Text-to-speech reads written words out loud for you to listen to.
Colour overlays put a coloured sheet over your reading material.
Chunking means breaking big amounts of information into smaller pieces.
In real life, you can chunk a long journey into smaller parts.
A common mistake is trying to read everything at once without breaks.

items: Don't read whole chapters at once.
Take short breaks every few pages.
Review what you just read immediately.

faq.q: Do I have to use text-to-speech for everything?
faq.a: No, you can use it for difficult passages or when you need to focus on listening first. You might also find it helpful to read some parts aloud yourself.
asks: Should I use this tool all the time?

faq.q: Are colour overlays good for everyone?
faq.a: They can help some people by reducing glare or making text less tiring to look at. However, what works for one person might not work for another.
asks: Will coloured sheets help my eyes?
Is this a permanent fix for reading?

faq.q: What is the best way to chunk notes?
faq.a: Try grouping related ideas together, like using headings or making bullet points for each small group. This keeps the information manageable.
asks: How do I break down big topics?
Can I use headings to chunk my study notes?

faq.q: If I use these strategies, will I never need help again?
faq.a: These are tools to help you learn better, not a cure. They are skills you practice to support your learning journey.
asks: Will I always need these tools?

faq.q: Can I use these tools for different subjects?
faq.a: Yes, these are general study skills. You can apply listening, colour filtering, and chunking to history, science, or English.
asks: Does this only work for English class?

facts: Text-to-speech technology reads digital text aloud for auditory support.
Colour overlays can help reduce visual stress when reading printed material.
Chunking involves dividing large amounts of information into smaller, digestible parts.
Listening to text read aloud can help build comprehension skills.

quiz.say: If you are reading a long article, what is the best strategy to use first?
quiz.why: Chunking helps you manage the large amount of information by breaking it into smaller, easier parts to process.

wrong.1: Colour overlays only help with visual comfort, not with organizing the information itself.
wrong.2: Text-to-speech is great for hearing the words, but it does not organize the ideas for you.
wrong.3: Reading everything quickly causes the brain to get overwhelmed and forget details.

quiz.say: When a book seems too bright to read from, which strategy might help?
quiz.why: Colour overlays filter the light, which can make the text appear less harsh or distracting to your eyes.

wrong.0: Reading it three times can cause eye strain without solving the underlying visual issue.
wrong.2: This helps with understanding but does not change the physical appearance of the printed page.
wrong.3: Chunking is about grouping ideas, not changing the visual quality of the page.

quiz.say: If you are learning about the three stages of the water cycle, what is the best way to study this?

options.show: Writing the whole cycle in one paragraph
options.say: Writing the whole cycle in one paragraph

quiz.why: You can use text-to-speech to hear the definition of each stage, and then chunk the process into three separate, manageable parts.

wrong.0: Only reading the labels might not give you enough detail about what happens in each stage.
wrong.1: Colour overlays help sight but do not teach you the sequence or the meaning of the stages.
wrong.2: Writing it all at once is too much information and is harder to remember than separate chunks.
